class_guess: Nested defect-walk counter (budget + round counter at two levels); 2-D residue-branching epoch map: cryptid-like
summary: A 0011 defect walks through 110 fields off a right counter; epochs reset via a 2-D map that branches on remainders
mechanism: Trips: the head shuttles between a 0011 defect (left wall) and a unary counter at the right end; each round trip moves the defect one 110 block right, and every 8 trips add 2 blocks to the counter (rule R1).

Two levels: the same walk also eats the second field (R2: x+16, y-8, z-6) and runs inside it (R3: a+4, b-2). When the active defect reaches the junk before the counter, the head sweeps to the left edge and a new epoch starts.

Epoch law (fitted, 22 resets to 1.6e10): N' ~ N + 1.22M, M' ~ 0.30N - 0.58M (eigenvalues 1.20, -0.78); phases end on remainders (mod 6, 8, 2) that pick the junk and the next branch. Halting needs D to read 0011 from its left; never seen.

template.note: W5-3 (our kill, BECv5 TM1 architecture): a defect walks through a periodic word while a right counter counts trips, plus a left-edge eat; one level, a binary counter, 5 residue cases, 1-D invariant 1 <= N <= 2p. Here the counter is unary, the same walk runs at two levels (R1, R3), and the epoch map is 2-D with eigenvalues 1.20 and -0.78, so a proof needs a 2-D band (e.g. 0.05N <= M <= 0.3N) plus a closed census of branch shapes. No upstream proof of this table; 291 is only in Eqv lemmas (Eqv.v TM44, Eqv_v3.v TM437).

strategy: Pre-registered stop: the epoch law divides fields and branches on remainders, so park as a cryptid candidate. If funded: build an exact epoch accelerator from R1-R3 and the reset branches, check it against direct runs to 2e10, then census the branch shapes far out to see whether they close.
risks: The branch set (J x R x phase, plus interleaved two-defect visits) may be large or not closed; 185 raw visit shapes by 1e8 (uncanonicalized).
The 2-D invariant band must survive residue perturbations; the -0.78 eigenvalue makes M/N oscillate (0.06..0.25 seen).
152 is only Eqv-linked (not the same table): a 291 proof transfers only through upstream Eqv lemmas resting on BBinf (two .v files).

checkpoint_questions.text: One visit: each black wedge is a round trip from the right counter to the 0011 defect. Does the wedges' left tip move right by one 3-cell block per trip?
Epochs: each new diagonal from the left edge starts an epoch. Do the epochs look like the same process repeating at a larger size each time?

Priority call (pre-registered 45-min go/no-go): the epoch law is a 2-D map that branches on remainders, though no branch is known to halt. Park it as a cryptid candidate, or fund one 2 h stage to build an exact epoch accelerator and census its branch shapes for closure?

stats.growth: epochs grow ~1.20x (fitted eigenvalue); span 94,226 at 1.63e10; 23 resets to 1.63e10, no halt

status_reason: Visit rules R1-R3 exact and validated (25/25 each). The epoch law is a 2-D piecewise-affine map (eigenvalues 1.20, -0.78) whose branches are picked by remainders mod 6/8/2: the pre-registered W6-3 stop rule. No halting branch is known; closure of the branch set is unproved.
